text: The book adds the Gibbons-Hawking-York term S_GHY = c⁴/(8πG) ∫_∂M K√|h| d³x to the Einstein-Hilbert action in order to:
choices: introduce the cosmological constant Λ into the field equations
make the action invariant under diffeomorphisms
obtain a well-posed variational problem requiring only δg^{μν} = 0 on the boundary ∂M
convert the metric variation into the Palatini (first-order) variation
explanation: The book explains that the Einstein-Hilbert action's second derivatives produce boundary terms that survive unless ∂_α δg^{μν} also vanishes on ∂M; the GHY term (with K the trace of the boundary's extrinsic curvature) cancels them so that only δg^{μν} = 0 is needed. It does not supply Λ, is not the source of diffeomorphism invariance, and is distinct from the Palatini approach.
